lead.title: Elomia Health acquires Earkick, the AI mental health companion founded between Zurich and San Francisco
lead.deck: Elomia Health, a conversational AI lab founded in 2019 by Ukrainian entrepreneur Taras Pohrebniak, is buying the Earkick app (more than 250,000 users, tracking mood, sleep and activity), its AI models and ongoing early access to its Mia21 memory engine; terms were not disclosed. The deal supports Elomia's shift, after a randomised controlled trial with the University of Pennsylvania, from a consumer app to API infrastructure for care organisations: AI mental health is entering its consolidation phase.

milestone.title: Égide Santé Réseau: Nouvelle-Aquitaine commits €3.4M to a sovereign regional network for health data exchange
milestone.summary: Regional e-health agency GRADeS ESEA is already piloting its secure network (fibre, regional DNS, file transfer, French intrusion probes and European firewalls, NIS2 audits) with seven hospitals, including the Bordeaux, Limoges and Poitiers university hospitals. Co-funding from the regional health agency ARS (€1.7M) and EU ERDF money via the Region (€1.7M) launches phase two: 18 more facilities, then another 25 between mid-2027 and mid-2028, for 50 health and social care sites in total.
milestone.why: A French region is building its own 'Renater for health', pitched as an alternative to non-European solutions: sovereignty and cybersecurity become shared infrastructure, opening doors for European operators and vendors (telecom aggregator Linkt is already a partner).

deal.thesis: Insight Partners leads the Series B, joined by Madrona, Bain Capital Ventures, South Park Commons and newcomer QuantumLight. Charta uses AI to audit medical charts before billing, inside the EHR (Charta for Providers), and sells the same engine to payers for risk adjustment and audits: a bet on shared 'ground truth' between providers and payers, upstream of disputes rather than after them.

brefsEurope.title: Sleep.ai (formerly SleepScore Labs) raises $5.3M from Treasure Coast Ventures, driven by its reimbursed programme in Germany
brefsEurope.summary: Its 'Dein Schlaf' programme, certified as prevention under Section 20 of Germany's Social Code Book V, is covered without a prescription for all 74 million statutory insurance members, with BARMER, AOK Niedersachsen, IKK Brandenburg und Berlin and BERGISCHE Krankenkasse; 25,000 active participants year to date. The platform normalises data from around 800 consumer wearables.

brefsEurope.company: Lancashire and South Cumbria NHS FT
brefsEurope.title: Lancashire and South Cumbria's Heidi pilot cuts out-of-hours clinical admin by 45%
brefsEurope.summary: In its 2025/26 digital report, the mental health trust says 78% of staff in the Heidi AI scribe pilot reported improved wellbeing; it is preparing a competitive ambient voice procurement (business case in November, completion targeted for March 2027). Its streamlined Rio EPR (15 core forms cut to five) is modelled to release about 26,700 clinical hours a year.

brefsEurope.title: Karolinska builds its AI governance around a Chief AI Officer and a national academy
brefsEurope.summary: Led by Chief AI Officer Joel Preger, the hospital is rolling out common guidelines and staff training through Health AI Academy Sweden, funded by the European Social Fund with Sweden's other university hospitals (SUHA). The region is preparing a new principal EHR and a shared data platform for the controlled deployment of AI.

brefsEurope.title: Lincolnshire's mental health trust surveys patients before rolling out its engagement portal
brefsEurope.summary: A survey ranks the features patients want (electronic appointments, secure messaging, carer access, letters in one place); the app, already connected to existing systems, will start in a few services. The trust relies on an EHR–ePMA integration engine from Interoperability Health (£77,273 until March 2028).

brefsIntl.title: Maven's virtual clinic goes in-network with more than 475 health plans, about 80% of commercially insured lives
brefsIntl.summary: Aetna, UnitedHealthcare and Blue Cross Blue Shield are among them: perimenopause, menopause and hormone care visits are covered at launch, with OB-GYNs and nutritionists to follow. The women's health leader, until now sold mainly through employers, opens a direct payer channel.

brefsIntl.title: Nordic Capital-backed Inovalon agrees to acquire e-prescribing specialist DrFirst
brefsIntl.summary: DrFirst, founded more than 25 years ago by James F. Chen, connects to more than 270 EHR interfaces; the combined group claims 71,000 pharmacies and 670,000 providers. Price undisclosed: the Swedish fund's portfolio company joins payer data with point-of-prescribing workflows.

brefsIntl.title: Randomised trial: alerting volunteer responders via the PulsePoint app does not improve cardiac arrest response
brefsIntl.summary: Across 355 public-location cardiac arrests (17,547 calls randomised from 2021 to 2026), bystander CPR or AED use reached 69% with alerts versus 72% without, and survival stayed around 21% in both arms. Preliminary results presented at the AHA Resuscitation Science Symposium, not yet peer-reviewed.

word.definition: An online programme or app that delivers the validated techniques of cognitive behavioural therapy (for insomnia, anxiety, depression) session by session, either self-guided or backed by a clinician.

parts.label: CBT protocol
parts.role: the clinical content (exercises, cognitive restructuring, sleep restriction)

parts.label: Digital engine
parts.role: personalisation and tracking (diary, questionnaires, conversational AI)

parts.label: Supervision and prescription
parts.role: the link to the care system (doctor, psychologist, reimbursement)

how.t: The patient is referred by a doctor, insurer or psychological therapy service, or self-refers; an initial questionnaire measures symptoms.
Over several weeks, the app delivers structured modules and daily exercises (sleep diary, exposure, reframing thoughts), adapted to the patient's answers.
Regular scores track progress; a psychologist or support AI helps between sessions, and more severe cases are escalated to human care.

word.why: dCBT is the most advanced digital therapeutics category in terms of market access: NICE recommends Sleepio as a cost-saving option for insomnia, Germany reimburses several HelloBetter programmes as DiGA, and in 2025 the US created Medicare codes for FDA-cleared digital mental health treatments. With generative AI, the frontier is moving to conversational companions that support patients between sessions, hence the ongoing consolidation (Elomia's acquisition of Earkick, reported on November 10).

startups.name: Big Health
startups.use: Sleepio and Daylight, digital CBT for insomnia and anxiety; Sleepio recommended by NICE, SleepioRx and DaylightRx cleared by the FDA; raised $23.7M in February 2026

startups.name: HelloBetter
startups.use: Prescription online therapy programmes reimbursed in Germany (Schlafen, Panik, Stress und Burnout, Diabetes…), backed by 30 clinical studies and more than 140,000 participants

startups.name: Limbic
startups.use: Limbic Care, an AI companion delivering CBT tools between sessions in NHS Talking Therapies services, 45% of which already use Limbic; Limbic Access carries a UKCA Class IIa mark
